- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and price is trending down, model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–2% or 0.5–1.0 point to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 3% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly negative and price is consolidating, model often over-optimistically forecasts upward; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently under-forecasts in early weeks (1–4) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast to account for lag.
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 in next 3–5 days.
